title: flaky_investigation — a box diagnosis of one queued flaky-test issue (more-local-inference 10)
description: What a local model concluded about one flaky test or CI job, from FlakeRadar's records and the code at main: the likely cause, the evidence, and the fix it proposes. It never reproduced the failure. `gate` checks the Input receipt, requires every cited file:line to exist in the checkout, and fails a comment over the 2,500 characters C9 gives this kind in background.md. `post` publishes it as the issue's flaky-investigation marker comment, which backlog's and ralph's `claim` copy into background.md for the run that takes the issue. _io is stamped by the server and is not part of this schema.

cause.description: The one class the evidence points at. `timing`: a sleep, a timeout, a race on the clock. `ordering`: the test depends on the order it runs in, or on another test having run. `shared-state`: a module-level, cached or database fixture two tests share. `resource`: a port, a lock, a file or a browser instance the test does not release. `network`: something outside the runner answered slowly or not at all. `environment`: a runner, image, OS or toolchain difference. `test-data`: a fixture, seed or generated value. `other` when the evidence does not single one out, and say so in `summary`.

summary.description: One to three plain sentences a human can act on: what the evidence shows and what you would change. Published verbatim on the issue.

evidence.description: What the conclusion rests on. `where` is path:line in the checkout, or the literal `flakeradar` for a fact from FlakeRadar's record, or `issue` for what the issue body says.

fix.description: The change you would make, as a proposal only: this run edits nothing and posts no branch. `where` is path:line, or `test` when the change is the test's own setup.

confidence.description: `high` only when a file:line in the checkout shows the mechanism. `low` when the evidence is FlakeRadar's failure texts alone.

reproduced.description: Always false: this run does not run the test. It reads FlakeRadar's records and the code. The field is here so nothing downstream can mistake the diagnosis for a reproduction.
